title: Wiretap-routed network loss with RFC 2198 recovery into WebRTC
objective: Emit a complete three-generation RTP/T.140 stream into a Sandia Wiretap-routed media path, drop only the middle RTP packet after Wiretap re-originates the UDP flow on the server side, and prove that the gateway reconstructs the missing T.140 generation from RFC 2198 redundancy before delivering the exact semantic stream to a real browser t140 data channel.

sourceProfile.sequence2: RFC2198 redundant B plus primary C

lossProfile.transport: Sandia Wiretap v0.9.0 routed media path

evidenceSeparation.source: proves all three RTP packets existed before the network fault
evidenceSeparation.network: proves one packet matching RTP sequence 1 was dropped after Wiretap server-side UDP re-origination
evidenceSeparation.gateway: proves only sequences 0 and 2 arrived and records recovery provenance
evidenceSeparation.sink: proves gateway forwarded the degraded RTP stream byte-for-byte unchanged
evidenceSeparation.browser: proves the recovered semantic stream reached a real RTCPeerConnection t140 data channel
evidenceSeparation.reducer: independently correlates all evidence planes and retains terminal verdict authority

securityModel.rule: The gateway decodes and reconstructs T.140 before re-originating it over WebRTC. Per-leg protection does not establish end-to-end encryption across the gateway.

requiredBeforeProven: network-induced loss at additional positions and burst patterns
out-of-order delivery and RFC 4103 waiting-timer behavior
insufficient-redundancy behavior producing the T.140 missing-text marker
production-representative VRS or gateway observations without provider-specific reducer branches

doesNotEstablish: end-to-end encryption across the media-terminating gateway
